# Euler Problem 66 Solution in Ada

This problem asks us to find the value of D ≤ 1000 for which the equation x² - Dy² = 1 has the largest minimal solution for x.

```ada
with Ada.Text_IO; use Ada.Text_IO;
with Ada.Integer_Text_IO; use Ada.Integer_Text_IO;
with Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers; use Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers;

procedure Euler_66 is
   
   type Big_Integer is new Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers.Big_Integer;
   
   function Is_Square(n : Big_Integer) return Boolean is
      Root : Big_Integer;
      Temp : Big_Integer;
   begin
      if n < 0 then
         return False;
      end if;
      
      if n = 0 or n = 1 then
         return True;
      end if;
      
      Root := Sqrt(n);
      Temp := Root * Root;
      
      -- Check if it's a perfect square
      if Temp = n then
         return True;
      elsif (Root + 1) * (Root + 1) = n then
         return True;
      elsif (Root - 1) * (Root - 1) = n then
         return True;
      else
         return False;
      end if;
   end Is_Square;
   
   function Continued_Fraction_Approximation(D : Big_Integer) return Big_Integer is
      -- Returns the minimal x value for x² - D*y² = 1 (Pell's equation)
      
      -- Handle special cases
      if Is_Square(D) then
         return 0;  -- No solution for perfect squares
      end if;
      
      -- Calculate continued fraction expansion of sqrt(D)
      -- We use the standard algorithm for solving Pell's equation
      
      type Fraction is record
         Num : Big_Integer;
         Den : Big_Integer;
      end record;
      
      P : Big_Integer := 0;
      Q : Big_Integer := 1;
      a : Big_Integer := Sqrt(D);
      a0 : Big_Integer := a;
      
      -- For the continued fraction expansion of sqrt(D)
      -- We use the recurrence relations:
      -- P[k+1] = a[k] * Q[k] - P[k]
      -- Q[k+1] = (D - P[k+1]^2) / Q[k]
      -- a[k+1] = (a0 + P[k+1]) / Q[k+1]
      
      h : array(0..1000) of Big_Integer := (others => 0);
      k : array(0..1000) of Big_Integer := (others => 0);
      
      -- Initial values
      h(0) := a0;
      k(0) := 1;
      
      if D = 2 then
         return h(0);
      end if;
      
      h(1) := a0 * h(0) + 1;
      k(1) := a0;
      
      -- Find the period of the continued fraction
      -- The minimal solution is found in the convergents
      i : Integer := 2;
      Period : Integer := 0;
      
      while True loop
         P := a * Q - P;
         Q := (D - P * P) / Q;
         a := (a0 + P) / Q;
         
         h(i) := a * h(i-1) + h(i-2);
         k(i) := a * k(i-1) + k(i-2);
         
         -- Check if we've found the fundamental solution
         -- For Pell's equation x² - D*y² = 1, we need to check if:
         -- h(i)² - D*k(i)² = 1
         declare
            Test : Big_Integer := h(i) * h(i) - D * k(i) * k(i);
         begin
            if Test = 1 then
               return h(i);
            end if;
         end;
         
         i := i + 1;
         exit when i > 1000;  -- Safety limit
      end loop;
      
      return h(i-1);  -- Return the last computed value as fallback
   end Continued_Fraction_Approximation;
   
   function Solve_Pell(D : Big_Integer) return Big_Integer is
      -- This implements a more robust Pell's equation solver using continued fractions
      Num : Big_Integer := 0;
      Den : Big_Integer := 1;
      a : Big_Integer := Sqrt(D);
      a0 : Big_Integer := a;
      
      -- For the convergents of sqrt(D) = [a₀; a₁, a₂, ...]
      h : array(0..2000) of Big_Integer := (others => 0);
      k : array(0..2000) of Big_Integer := (others => 0);
      
      -- Initial convergents
      h(0) := a0;
      k(0) := 1;
      
      if D = 2 then
         return h(0);
      end if;
      
      h(1) := a0 * h(0) + 1;
      k(1) := a0;
      
      -- Continue until we find a solution to x² - D*y² = 1
      i : Integer := 2;
      
      while True loop
         declare
            P : Big_Integer := 0;
            Q : Big_Integer := 1;
            a_new : Big_Integer := 0;
            Test : Big_Integer := 0;
         begin
            -- Calculate the next term in continued fraction expansion
            P := a * Den - Num;
            Q := (D - P * P) / Den;
            a_new := (a0 + P) / Q;
            
            -- Update numerator and denominator for next iteration
            Num := P;
            Den := Q;
            a := a_new;
            
            -- Calculate the next convergent
            h(i) := a * h(i-1) + h(i-2);
            k(i) := a * k(i-1) + k(i-2);
            
            -- Check if this is a solution to Pell's equation
            Test := h(i) * h(i) - D * k(i) * k(i);
            if Test = 1 then
               return h(i);
            end if;
            
            i := i + 1;
            exit when i > 2000;  -- Safety limit
         end;
      end loop;
      
      return h(i-1);  -- Fallback
   end Solve_Pell;
   
   Max_X : Big_Integer := 0;
   Best_D : Integer := 0;
   
begin
   for D in 2..1000 loop
      declare
         X : Big_Integer;
      begin
         -- Skip perfect squares
         if not Is_Square(D) then
            X := Solve_Pell(D);
            if X > Max_X then
               Max_X := X;
               Best_D := D;
            end if;
         end if;
      end;
   end loop;
   
   Put_Line("The value of D ≤ 1000 for which the equation x² - Dy² = 1 has the largest minimal solution is:");
   Put(Best_D); Put_Line("");
   Put_Line("The minimal x solution is:");  
   Put(Max_X); Put_Line("");
end Euler_66;
```

with Ada.Text_IO; use Ada.Text_IO;
with Ada.Integer_Text_IO; use Ada.Integer_Text_IO;
with Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers; use Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers;

procedure Euler_66 is
   
   type Big_Integer is new Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers.Big_Integer;
   
   function Is_Perfect_Square(n : Big_Integer) return Boolean is
      Root : Big_Integer := Sqrt(n);
   begin
      if Root * Root = n then
         return True;
      else
         return False;
      end if;
   end Is_Perfect_Square;
   
   function Solve_Pell(D : Integer) return Big_Integer is
      -- Find minimal solution to x² - D*y² = 1 using continued fractions
      A0, A, P, Q, P0, Q0 : Big_Integer;
      H0, H1, K0, K1 : Big_Integer := 0;
      H, K : Big_Integer;
      
      -- Initialize
      A0 := Sqrt(D);
      P := A0;
      Q := 1;
      P0 := 0;
      Q0 := 1;
      
      -- Initial convergents
      H0 := A0;
      K0 := 1;
      H1 := A0 * A0 + 1;
      K1 := A0;
      
      H := H1;
      K := K1;
      
      -- Continue until we find solution
      for i in 2..5000 loop
         P := A * Q - P;
         Q := (D - P * P) / Q;
         A := (A0 + P) / Q;
         
         H := A * H1 + H0;
         K := A * K1 + K0;
         
         -- Check if we found solution to Pell's equation
         if H * H - Big_Integer(D) * K * K = 1 then
            return H;
         end if;
         
         -- Update for next iteration
         H0 := H1;
         K0 := K1;
         H1 := H;
         K1 := K;
      end loop;
      
      return 0;  -- No solution found
   end Solve_Pell;
   
   Max_X : Big_Integer := 0;
   Best_D : Integer := 0;
   
begin
   for D in 2..1000 loop
      if not Is_Perfect_Square(D) then
         declare
            X : Big_Integer := Solve_Pell(D);
         begin
            if X > Max_X then
               Max_X := X;
               Best_D := D;
            end if;
         end;
      end if;
   end loop;
   
   Put_Line("Answer: D = "); Put(Best_D); New_Line;
   Put_Line("Minimal x = "); Put(Max_X); New_Line;
end Euler_66;

```ada
with Ada.Text_IO; use Ada.Text_IO;
with Ada.Integer_Text_IO; use Ada.Integer_Text_IO;
with Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers; use Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers;

procedure Euler_66 is
   
   type Big_Integer is new Ada.Numerics.Big_Integers.Big_Integer;
   
   function Is_Perfect_Square(n : Big_Integer) return Boolean is
      Root : Big_Integer := Sqrt(n);
   begin
      return Root * Root = n;
   end Is_Perfect_Square;
   
   function Find_Min_Solution(D : Integer) return Big_Integer is
      -- Using continued fraction method to solve Pell's equation x² - D*y² = 1
      A0, A, P, Q : Big_Integer := 0;
      H0, H1, K0, K1 : Big_Integer := 0;
      H, K : Big_Integer := 0;
      
   begin
      -- Special case for perfect squares
      if Is_Perfect_Square(D) then
         return 0;
      end if;
      
      -- Initialize continued fraction
      A0 := Sqrt(D);
      P := A0;
      Q := 1;
      
      -- Initialize convergents
      H0 := 1;
      K0 := 0;
      H1 := A0;
      K1 := 1;
      
      H := H1;
      K := K1;
      
      -- Continue until we find solution to x² - D*y² = 1
      loop
         P := A * Q - P;
         Q := (D - P * P) / Q;
         A := (A0 + P) / Q;
         
         H := A * H1 + H0;
         K := A * K1 + K0;
         
         -- Check if we found a solution
         if H * H - Big_Integer(D) * K * K = 1 then
            return H;
         end if;
         
         -- Update for next iteration
         H0 := H1;
         K0 := K1;
         H1 := H;
         K1 := K;
      end loop;
      
      return 0;
   end Find_Min_Solution;
   
   Max_X : Big_Integer := 0;
   Best_D : Integer := 0;
   
begin
   for D in 2..1000 loop
      declare
         X : Big_Integer := Find_Min_Solution(D);
      begin
         if X /= 0 and then X > Max_X then
            Max_X := X;
            Best_D := D;
         end if;
      end;
   end loop;
   
   Put_Line("The value of D ≤ 1000 for which x² - Dy² = 1 has the largest minimal solution:");
   Put(Best_D); New_Line;
   Put_Line("The minimal x value is:");  
   Put(Max_X); New_Line;
end Euler_66;
```

This Ada program solves Euler Problem 66 by:
1. Finding the minimal solution (x, y) to Pell's equation x² - Dy² = 1 for each D from 2 to 1000
2. Using continued fraction expansion to efficiently compute solutions
3. Tracking the maximum x value among all valid D values
4. Outputting the result
